data.title: Before the Wall Street bell-ringing ceremony | On-chain answer already given: The truth about the Anthropic price spread
data.description: At 11:48 AM Eastern Time on November 19, 2026, the Nasdaq opening bell rang for Anthropic (stock code: ANT). After a two-hour and eighteen-minute pre-market auction, the first traded price settled at $111.50, a 34.3% increase from the offering price of $83, briefly pushing its market capitalization past the $2 trillion mark. With its initial fundraising of $81.34 billion, Anthropic surpassed SpaceX, setting a new record for the highest-grossing IPO in global capital markets. Just one minute before the official opening, the pre-market price for ANT contracts on the decentralized perpetual contract trading platform Hyperliquid stopped at $111. Two seemingly unrelated markets differed in price by a mere 50 cents. Overnight, the crypto market appeared to have taken over Wall Street's pricing power. But behind this tiny 50-cent difference lies a truth far more complex than "precise pricing." Before Wall Street even opened, the blockchain was already a frenzy. In the past, unicorn IPOs were a highly closed game. Investment banks handled the book-building, institutional investors received the majority of the allocation, and ordinary investors could only trade after the stock was listed. Company valuations could rise steadily in the primary market, but a publicly available, continuous, and participatory price often only appeared on the day of the listing. Pre-market contracts are rewriting this order. Glassnode data shows that Anthropic's cumulative pre-market contract notional trading volume in the 45 days leading up to its IPO reached a staggering $9.5 billion, a 144% increase compared to SpaceX's $3.9 billion during the same period, setting a new record for pre-market trading. According to Castle Labs data, as of November 19th, the 24-hour trading volume of the Anthropic pre-market contract on Entropy.io alone on Hyperliquid reached approximately $531 million, with open interest reaching $496 million at one point, nearly double the peak open interest before SpaceX's IPO. A new market division of labor is emerging. Wall Street still controls stock issuance and allocation, while the crypto market has taken over the role of "pre-market trading." Before the official opening of the stock market, it allows global investors to buy and sell unicorn price expectations using stablecoins. IPOs are no longer just a game of price inquiries and allocations among institutional investors, but are beginning to become an open and continuous trading market. The truth behind the 0.2% error: "Copying homework" from Nasdaq. While the pre-market market is rapidly expanding, the price difference between on-chain contracts and traditional markets seems to be narrowing significantly. According to calculations by Eliezer Ndinga, Head of Research at 21Shares, the pre-market price of ANT contracts on Hyperliquid differed from its Nasdaq first-minute trading price by only 0.2%, and the average price difference between the two further narrowed to about 0.1% after the opening. Even using the official Nasdaq opening price of $111.50, the error was only 0.5%. If you only observe the two minutes before and after the opening, the crypto market seems to have completed "precise pricing" before Nasdaq. But if you extend the timeline, the story changes. At 4:35 PM Eastern Time on November 18th, the night before the IPO pricing, the pre-market ANT contract on Hyperliquid was still around $98, 12.11% below the opening price the next day. It wasn't until the morning of November 19th that Nasdaq's auction window began releasing price signals at $100, $104, and $110, and the on-chain price followed suit, finally reaching $110.48 four minutes before the opening (11:44 AM Eastern Time), 0.91% below the first traded price. The price difference within 1% is less a sign of the crypto market having foresight and more a result of traders meticulously tracking the Nasdaq pre-market auction on Bloomberg terminals. It's more like a cross-market information relay rather than a one-sided pre-pricing by the crypto market. In the early stages of pre-market contracts, prices reflected a vague consensus in the market regarding the valuation of the underlying asset. As prospectuses, offering price ranges, and oversubscription results during roadshows were gradually disclosed, market expectations were continuously revised. During the call auction phase, the real-time price indication from the traditional market became the most direct anchor, guiding pre-market prices to converge. The so-called "precise pricing" in the crypto market essentially means that it opened a tradable market earlier, and subsequently, as information became more transparent, prices continued to converge towards the true price. Pre-market market performance: Correct direction doesn't guarantee accurate price. Anthropic's "perfect synchronization" is more like an exceptional case than a replicable pattern. Looking back at historical pre-IPO cases, pre-market contracts haven't performed as well as ANT. Of the eight IPOs analyzed by Grayscale, pre-market contracts achieved a 7/8 accuracy rate in predicting the opening direction on the first day. All five stocks that Trade.xyz completed conversions also conformed to the pattern of "issue price lower than the previous night's contract price, opening price higher than the issue price." From a directional perspective, pre-market contracts serve as a reliable "sentiment thermometer." However, when applied to price, the error becomes dramatically amplified. The most typical counterexample is SpaceX. On the eve of its IPO in June, the SpaceX pre-market contract on Hyperliquid closed at $172.84, implying a 28% first-day gain; however, the Nasdaq opened at only $150 the following day, meaning the contract still deviated from the actual opening price by about 6% even in the last minute before opening. Cerebras and Quantumuum performed even worse, remaining deeply trapped below their IPO prices for extended periods after listing. Even Anthropic, after opening high at $111.50, quickly fell back, closing its first day at $97.17. If an average investor had focused on the on-chain price of $110 and rushed into the Nasdaq opening price, they would have suffered a 12.85% unrealized loss in just four hours. The most memorable aspect of Anthropic's listing day wasn't the small price difference of less than 1% in the pre-market market. The crypto market hasn't proven itself to know better than Wall Street how much an AI giant is worth, but it has transformed the previously closed IPO pricing process, accessible only to a select few, into an open, continuous market where everyone can participate. The debate over the value of a unicorn is no longer confined to investment banks' closed-door roadshows. This is an extension of pricing power; Wall Street issues the shares, while the crypto market trades in the anticipation. Ultimately, the answer lies in the real money after the market opens. (Author: Jae, PANews)

data.title: Apple Takes Aim At OpenAI And Anthropic With New Autonomous AI Agent Planned For 2027
data.description:
Apple is preparing a major push into autonomous artificial intelligence, developing an AI agent capable of controlling devices, browsing the internet, operating applications, and writing code as it looks to challenge OpenAI and Anthropic.

NEW: Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent with computer-use capabilities, including device control, app interactions, web browsing and coding. The effort goes well beyond Siri and aims to compete with Meta’s Muse, ChatGPT’s Dots and Claude Code. https://t.co/lRvi4NJ3zk

— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) November 19, 2026

The company's ambitions emerged through recent job listings published on its website, including a recruitment notice for a Senior Engineering Manager. The listings suggest Apple is moving beyond its traditional approach of integrating AI features into its operating systems toward developing a proactive assistant capable of using a computer "like a competent person would."

Another Apple listing, for a senior manager in its Agentic AI – Proactive team, describes "general-purpose computer-use agents" that "coordinate specialized sub-agents." Andrew Curran’s screenshot shows it posted 17 Nov; Apple’s page now says the role is no longer available.

— Gennaro (@fourweekmba) November 20, 2026

The project marks a significant shift in Apple's AI strategy, particularly as competitors race to establish dominance in the emerging autonomous AI agent market. However, with the initiative still in its early stages and a launch not expected before the end of 2027, Apple faces the challenge of proving it can catch up with established players.

Apple Develops Autonomous AI Agent to Challenge OpenAI and Anthropic

Apple's latest recruitment efforts reveal ambitions to develop an AI assistant capable of performing tasks independently across digital environments.

According to the job descriptions, the proposed agent would be able to operate applications, interact with device interfaces, conduct autonomous web searches, and write or debug code. The broader objective is to create an AI system that can navigate software and complete tasks on behalf of users rather than simply responding to instructions.

According to Bloomberg, the project is still in its early development stages and is being overseen under new CEO John Ternus. It is not expected to reach the market before the end of 2027.

The agent push comes as new Apple CEO John Ternus presses software chief Craig Federighi to move faster and take a more ambitious approach to AI. The company is still in the early stages of developing the agent, but has eyed a launch as soon as the end of 2027.

— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) November 19, 2026

The initiative puts Apple in direct competition with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta, which are also developing autonomous AI agents. OpenAI's Dots, Anthropic's Duet, and Meta's Muse represent competing efforts to establish AI systems capable of taking on increasingly complex tasks.

🚨 ALERT: Meta’s Muse AI agent reportedly accessed private messages and shared incorrect financial data, raising privacy concerns, per Reuters. https://t.co/acw2Br6Sr0

— Cointelegraph (@Cointelegraph) November 19, 2026

For Apple, the stakes extend beyond introducing another AI-powered feature. The company is attempting to secure a position in what could become the next major evolution of human-computer interaction, where users increasingly rely on AI agents to navigate applications, access information, and complete everyday tasks.

Siri's Legacy Raises Questions About Apple's AI Ambitions

Despite Apple's ambitions, its latest AI initiative has already attracted skepticism from technology observers.

Following the emergence of the job listings, several users on X questioned whether Apple could deliver on its promises, pointing to Siri's long history of struggling to meet expectations. For critics, the company risks entering the autonomous AI race after competitors have already established a technological lead.

🚨 ALERT: Meta’s Muse AI agent reportedly accessed private messages and shared incorrect financial data, raising privacy concerns, per Reuters. https://t.co/acw2Br6Sr0

— Cointelegraph (@Cointelegraph) November 19, 2026

Building an AI agent capable of independently accessing files, adjusting settings, navigating browsers, and interacting with applications also presents significant technical challenges. Unlike conventional chatbots, autonomous agents must execute tasks reliably while avoiding mistakes that could compromise user data or device security.

Apple does have a potential advantage through its control over its hardware, processors, and operating systems. Its extensive iPhone, Mac, and iPad ecosystem could provide a foundation for integrating an AI agent across multiple devices.

A Grok Bot user says their bot rebooked a cancelled flight by phone while they waited in a 187-person line, and Elon Musk shared it. → It sat on hold, told the agent up front it was an AI, and got a 7:40 AM seat plus a hotel and meals → It asked before paying $49 for an aisle seat → It ran on 3 rules: say you're an AI, ask only for what's owed, ask before spending https://t.co/57i3VYdJ62

— 0xMarioNawfal (@RoundtableSpace) November 15, 2026

However, that advantage alone may not be enough. Apple will need to demonstrate that its technology can perform complex tasks reliably rather than simply showcase impressive capabilities in controlled demonstrations.

Apple's $5.1 Trillion Valuation Faces a New AI Challenge

Apple's push into autonomous AI comes at a particularly important moment for the company, which has enjoyed strong stock market performance despite taking a more measured approach to AI investments than some of its competitors.

According to data cited from Bloomberg Línea, Apple's shares have gained 29% over the year, making it the strongest performer among the Magnificent Seven technology companies. The rally also helped push its market capitalization to approximately $5.1 trillion.

Apple ($AAPL) ranked as the second most under-owned mega-cap stock exiting 3Q26, with active institutional portfolio weighting lagging its S&P 500 benchmark by -2.54%. The under-ownership spread widened by 21 basis points quarter-over-quarter as institutional allocators maintained cautious positioning heading into the next hardware replacement cycle. Furthermore, with NVIDIA shares having fallen 32% over the subsequent 45 days while Apple gained 6%, analysts observe that Apple has plausibly become the single most under-owned mega-cap holding in real-time positioning. This structural underweight reflects persistent investor skepticism regarding consumer hardware upgrade velocity, yet historical technical analysis shows that extreme benchmark under-ownership frequently creates substantial upward pressure as portfolio managers rebalance. On the operating front, aged installed base dynamics indicate peaking replacement cycles that can sustain mid-teens hardware growth across global markets. Sell-side models project Apple can generate FY27 EPS of $9.84 and FY28 EPS of $10.65, supported by mid-teens Products expansion and steady ~10% Services revenue growth. However, rising memory input costs present a tangible near-term margin headwind: analysts estimate consolidated gross margin will contract from 48.8% in FY26 to 46.4% in FY27 before pricing power and supply-chain negotiations mitigate component inflation. The primary operational catalyst to monitor is whether new device form factors and artificial intelligence software capabilities successfully accelerate high-end iPhone 17 upgrade intentions amidst consumer demand elasticity. #MarketStrategy #Investing Report date: 2026-11-17

— 456X (@OptionKing666) November 19, 2026

Apple's more cautious spending strategy has helped distinguish it from technology companies committing enormous sums to AI infrastructure and cloud computing. However, entering the autonomous AI agent market could force the company to reconsider how aggressively it invests in the technology.

The challenge will be finding a balance between developing competitive AI capabilities and maintaining the cost discipline that has helped support investor confidence.

Ultimately, Apple's latest initiative highlights how autonomous AI agents are emerging as a major battleground for the technology industry. OpenAI and Anthropic have already made significant moves into the space, and Apple now appears determined to secure its own position.

AI VS. AI | Cybersecurity researchers used artificial intelligence to uncover a major flaw in Java software before hackers could exploit it — but experts warn bad actors are using the same technology to find vulnerabilities first. https://t.co/TzFVaGtDtm

— WPEC CBS12 News (@CBS12) November 20, 2026

Whether the company can overcome years of criticism surrounding Siri and deliver an AI assistant capable of competing with its rivals remains to be seen. With a potential launch still years away, Apple has time to develop its technology, but the race to control the next generation of AI-powered software interfaces is already underway.

data.title: South Korean Man Accused Of Using AI To Cheat In Law Entrance Exam Found Dead At Seoul Motel
data.description:
A South Korean man who gained public attention for achieving a perfect score in a national law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul, hours before he was due to livestream a test to defend himself against allegations of AI-assisted cheating.

Lee Jin-woo, 32, was found unconscious at a motel near Cheonho Station on 19 November after failing to appear for the scheduled livestream.

🚨#SOUTHKOREA PERFECT LEET SCORER FOUND DEAD

Lee Jin-woo, 32, had promised to solve the national college entrance exam live on November 19 to prove his abilities & address cheating allegations

He never showed up. Police later found him in cardiac arrest at a Seoul motel#이진우pic.twitter.com/ZR0bFCUtzj

— GlobeUpdate (@Globupdate) November 19, 2026

Perfect Exam Results Sparked AI Cheating Suspicions

Lee's academic achievements attracted attention after he went from performing poorly in South Korea's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) to scoring almost perfectly in 2025 and gaining admission to Seoul National University's dentistry programme.

He later achieved a perfect score in the 2026 Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET), published a book titled "Brain Accelerator" and began coaching students preparing for examinations.

However, suspicions emerged after viewers noticed unusual answer corrections in his LEET examination booklet, which he showed on a YouTube channel in October.

The pattern raised speculation that he might have copied answers from an external source, potentially AI, although this did not establish that cheating had occurred.

Questions also emerged over his previous examination results, prompting further scrutiny of his academic claims.

The second case, and the most controversial, involves Lee Jin-woo (born 1994), the first person ever to earn a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET), Korea’s law school admission test. The LEET has 70 questions, and reportedly no one had achieved a perfect… pic.twitter.com/LyzyVMOHNm

— Milkyway (@J4075648487243) November 16, 2026

Lee Failed To Appear For Public Livestream

Lee had agreed to solve Korean-language questions from the 2026 CSAT in real time to prove his abilities.

The livestream was scheduled for 8am on 19 November and attracted more than 400,000 viewers.

He had told a media outlet the previous evening,

"I will demonstrate my abilities through a public test and put the allegations to rest."

🚨 LEE JIN-WOO'S LAST KNOWN INTERVIEW DRAWS ATTENTION AFTER HIS DEATH

Viewers are dissecting his answers, movements & demeanour, reigniting debate over the allegations surrounding his perfect LEET score#LeeJinwoo#이진우#SouthKorea#LEEThttps://t.co/ZlbcBB2PIQpic.twitter.com/MZUhfVXU1P

— GlobeUpdate (@Globupdate) November 19, 2026

However, he failed to arrive, and organisers cancelled the exercise at 8:35am.

Police began searching for him after receiving a report expressing concern for his safety at 8:42am.

Investigators traced his movements between motels before finding him dead at around 1.10pm.

A note recovered from his room reportedly read,

"My body and mind are exhausted."

It did not mention the cheating allegations or contain an apology.

Police said an autopsy and further investigations would establish the cause of death.

Police Investigation Into Alleged Exam Fraud Continues

The controversy also brought attention to Lee's previous criminal convictions.

In 2022, he received an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for two years, for deliberately causing taxi accidents and extorting money from drivers.

He later received an additional six-month sentence for repeating similar offences against five people.

Before his death, two criminal complaints had been filed over allegations that he used AI to cheat in the CSAT and LEET, potentially falsified examination records and misled buyers of his study book and services.

Although Lee's death is expected to end criminal proceedings against him, South Korean police said they would continue investigating the allegations and whether anyone else was involved.

The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said the investigation would continue "to confirm the substantive truth".

This is reportedly the last CCTV footage of Lee Jin-woo before his death. He was expected to publicly address the allegations surrounding his perfect LEET score, but instead, news of his death emerged.#이진우https://t.co/WSFRvxa9Bypic.twitter.com/3LtfSRv8DJ

— Favored🌷 (@Your_favored) November 19, 2026

data.title: What does Democratic control of Congress mean for digital assets after the midterm elections?
data.description:
Author: Katrina Paglia, Chief Legal Officer of Pantera; Source: Pantera November Blockchain Investor Letter; Compiled by: Jinse Finance Claw

The Democrats won control of both houses of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, flipping the House and taking the Senate by a large margin—multiple media outlets have called it one of the biggest seat swings in decades.

This result was primarily driven by economic issues and the aftermath of the Iran war, with digital asset policy being a secondary factor, but it has reshaped the political landscape of the entire industry; and the industry's core legislative priority—a federal market structure bill—has been under negotiation in this landscape for nearly three years.

Source: Digital asset position ratings from Stand With Crypto, as of November 16, 2026; unrated members are listed as "Unrated". Election results and house seats are from the Associated Press, as of 3:09 PM ET on November 19, 2026. Senate counts include two independent senators operating with the Democratic caucus. Stand With Crypto's party-to-party data may differ from the Associated Press count by one House seat. What Changes Have Occurred in Congress? As of November 19, the Associated Press reported that Democrats won 257 seats in the House of Representatives, Republicans 172, and 6 seats remain undecided. Hakeem Jeffries is expected to succeed Mike Johnson as Speaker. In the Senate, the Associated Press reported that Democrats held 56 seats (including two independent senators operating with the Democratic caucus) and Republicans 44. This result gives Democrats control of the House Financial Services Committee and the Senate Banking Committee for the last two years of the Trump administration—these two committees are responsible for drafting legislation on the structure of the digital asset market. However, Trump retains the power to veto any bill submitted to the president's desk. The new Congress is also unusually inexperienced. When the 120th Congress is sworn in on January 3, 2027, at least 120 of the 535 seats in the House and Senate (approximately 22%, which could rise as the results of the final few elections are announced) will be filled by newly elected members, representing one of the largest groups of newly elected members in decades. This personnel change has both advantages and disadvantages, but overall it is a mildly positive for the industry. A significant portion of the newly elected members have no voting history on digital asset issues and do not possess the deeply entrenched, personally hostile stances of some outgoing members; this allows for greater flexibility in developing sound policies from scratch, rather than engaging in battles with established opposition forces.

A New Path for the CLARITY Act

The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act passed the House of Representatives by a large margin in July 2025 with bipartisan support, but stalled in the Senate Banking Committee due to ethical provisions concerning the president's and members' personal digital asset holdings; Democratic senators such as Kirsten Gillibrand have warned about this for months.

Now that Democrats control both houses, the bill is unlikely to advance with the existing version already passed in the House. It has been reported that House Democrats are discussing expanding Representative Maxine Waters' Crypto Investors Consumer Rights Act into their own broader market structure framework, rather than abandoning the effort altogether.

The industry's investment of approximately $233 million in the midterm elections did not translate into lasting control over the outcome; the potential terms of any final agreement—including stronger conflict-of-interest provisions for the president and a greater emphasis on investor protection compared to the CFTC-centric approach of the House bill—are likely to shift in the Democratic direction. Other regulatory clues to watch: Not everything is in flux. The GENIUS Act—the stablecoin framework to be signed into law in 2025—is already in place, and its implementing rules at the Treasury and banking regulator levels will continue to be developed regardless of which party controls Congress. The Senate's power to confirm the leadership of the SEC and CFTC now rests with committees controlled by Democrats, which will impact the next round of committee vacancies, but will not change the current Trump-appointed agency heads before 2029. The more direct impact lies in the tone. A Congress focused on overseeing the current administration's own digital asset initiatives (including the president's meme and token projects) is likely to maintain this scrutiny through hearings and investigations, even if it fails to legislate—a point several Democrats have cited as a reason for the breakdown in market structure negotiations. What does this mean for crypto? The baseline scenario is delay and renegotiation, not a reversal. The stablecoin framework has been maintained, but comprehensive federal market structure legislation—the rulebook that will ultimately clarify the SEC and CFTC's jurisdiction over most tokens—seems unlikely to pass before the next Congress convenes in 2027, and is likely to be delayed even further. This means the current landscape, cobbled together by SEC enforcement, CFTC jurisdiction, and state-level money transfer laws, will persist longer than the industry expects. Therefore, we should continue to assess and place new positions according to existing rules (rather than the rules we expect to arrive soon). We will continue to monitor the House Democrats' market structure alternatives and the development of ethics provisions in the next Congress.

data.title: Solana validators decreased by 64% in less than three years: Decentralization is no longer a necessity.
data.description:
Author: r2Jamong Source: X, @r2Jamong Translation: Shan Ouba, Jinse Finance

Solana's active validator count has decreased by 64% in less than three years, from 1,963 on December 28, 2023 to 701 on November 15, 2026. However, the Solana Foundation continues to scale back the delegation program that once helped maintain the validator base. Are the long-standing goals of decentralization and wider distribution in blockchain networks losing their appeal?

Focus of Exits Contributed to Validators with Less Staking

Of the 1,963 validators who held staked data in December 2023, 1,713 left. Of the 701 validators supporting the network at the end of the period, 250 were from the original group, and 451 were newcomers. To determine what these exits mean for a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) network, it's necessary to understand two things simultaneously: how many validators left, and what happened to their staking.

Of the top 100 validators by staking volume in December 2023, only 12 left. None of these 12 voting accounts registered the operator's name, so some operators may have simply changed accounts. Of the 1,663 validators ranked 301st and below, 95% have left, with most small validators relying on small staking amounts shutting down their nodes.

During the same period, Solana's total staking volume increased by approximately 11%, from 387.2 million SOL to 429.33 million SOL. The proportion of staking to total supply remained almost unchanged, slightly decreasing from approximately 68% to 67%.

The Foundation reduced delegation of approximately 41 million SOL, meaning that staking from other sources increased by approximately 83 million SOL.

Measured by the number of validators, Solana became less decentralized and less decentralized; however, the security it gained from staking SOL remained.

Foundation Reduces Delegation Program

Including validators who joined and left during the period, a total of 2,576 validators left. Of these, 1,280 had staked less than 20% of their peak amount before ceasing operations. Loss of delegated staking directly reduces revenue and makes it harder to cover node operating costs. Given Solana's high hardware requirements, a decline in revenue is enough to force a validator to shut down.

Of the departing validators, 1,243 held between 50,000 and 100,000 SOL at their peak. Staking rankings provide clues as to why so many validators maintained this level. In December 2023, approximately 70% of the total staking by the 700 validators ranked 301st to 1000th came from the Solana Foundation Delegated Program (SFDP). The way the Foundation allocates staking may also explain why a large number of validators in this group held between 60,000 and 70,000 SOL. The timing of these exits also coincides with adjustments to the Foundation's delegation rules. The first half of 2024 saw 865 exits, the highest number for a half-year. The revised rules took effect on the 578th epoch in February 2024. In the second half of 2025, another 451 validators left. In October of that year, the foundation began reducing the matching ratio from 1:1 to 0.5:1, and the matching cap from 100,000 SOL to 50,000 SOL. According to the foundation, SFDP's share of total staking had decreased from approximately 44.4% at launch to approximately 5.9% in November 2025. This trend illustrates that as the foundation reduces staking subsidies, validators who cannot attract sufficient external staking or maintain operations through self-delegation are gradually leaving the system. Validators who are most unable to replace foundation-delegated operators with their own SOL or external delegation are also the most likely to fail to sustain their nodes. What does a mature PoS network look like? What exactly do distribution and decentralization mean? A network with more validators has a wider physical distribution and a higher degree of decentralization. However, if most of their staking comes from the same foundation, political power remains centralized. On Solana, the foundation's staking share has decreased significantly, while staking outside the foundation is increasing. In this sense, power distribution is broader than before. The network is less decentralized in terms of the number of nodes, but the power to decide "who can afford to be a validator" has shifted from the foundation to the market. With the decrease in the proportion of staking provided by the foundation, validators rely more on the SOL they can stake and the delegation they obtain from others. As PoS networks mature, external delegators will naturally take over the foundation's role in early supply staking.

The Old Narrative of Distribution and Decentralization

For many, decentralization and distribution have long been the standards for measuring the value of blockchains. Today, both as ends in themselves are losing weight.

Among the densely emerging layer-one blockchains, only a few have survived. Each survivor can give its own unique reasons, and they now see relying on these distinctive advantages as the best opportunity for survival.

Trustlessness and censorship resistance remain Ethereum's highest priorities, and Ethereum already has means beyond decentralization and distribution to maintain these two points.

It has already reduced the number of validators through validator consolidation; after transitioning to zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs, a small number of operators with high-performance hardware will handle most of the block production and proof generation. As long as trustlessness and censorship resistance remain, Ethereum has little reason to decentralize every part of the network. Solana aims to build an internet capital market where people can trade any asset. Such markets require infrastructure operators capable of maintaining low latency and high throughput even during surges in transaction volume. Maintaining a large validator set involves costs and trade-offs, and Solana has chosen to bear fewer costs than in the past. Distribution and decentralization once provided blockchain networks with a way to prove "why people need it." As the hype subsided, networks found other reasons to use them and began to recalculate the true value of decentralization. Decentralization is no longer a creed for every blockchain.

data.title: Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet To Exit After 9 Years As AI Cybersecurity Threats Mount
data.description:
Ledger chief technology officer Charles Guillemet is preparing to leave the cryptocurrency hardware wallet manufacturer at the end of 2026, bringing his nine-year tenure at the company to a close as cybersecurity threats become increasingly sophisticated.

In a LinkedIn post on Thursday, Guillemet announced that he would depart after helping shape Ledger's security operations and establishing its Donjon security laboratory. He joined the company as chief security officer in December 2017, approximately three years after its founding, before becoming CTO.

Personal update: I’ll be leaving @ledger at the end of 2026. After nine years, those words are strange to type. I joined as CSO in December 2017. No desks, no team, just a blank page. I built the @DonjonLedger, our attack lab. Since then it has broken smartphone secure-boot chains, responsibly disclosed vulnerabilities in hardware, software, infrastructure across the industry, pushed research into post-quantum cryptography and AI-driven security... Later, as CTO, I helped grow Ledger from a small startup into a unicorn. Ledger has now sold more than 8 million signers in 180 countries, and they protect roughly 20% of the world’s crypto assets. We built a full line of signers (Ledger Nano, Stax, Flex, Gen5 and Atom), the Ledger Wallet app, and Ledger Enterprise, which now serves 100+ financial institutions and brands. I’m proud of all of it. I learned a lot along the way. In nine years, crypto went from a niche to infrastructure for modern finance, and cryptography made fifty years of progress in ten. Bitcoin is still permissionless money, and we still need it. The threat landscape changed too. AI is making attacks cheaper, faster and easier to scale; The Donjon now uses AI to hunt bugs, and attackers do the same. The question we spent a decade answering for crypto (how do you protect what matters when any device can be compromised?) is now a question for every company, every AI agent and every government. Thank you to @_pgauthier and the early team for trusting me with that blank page. To all the teams: you are exceptional, and it has been an honor to build with you. We’ve been preparing this transition for many months, so Ledger’s teams, partners and roadmaps are ready. I’m bullish on Ledger’s future. As for me, I’m building something new. I’m gonna dedicate my time to solving this security mess. More very soon. Stay safe. Stay honest about your trust assumptions.

— Charles Guillemet (@P3b7_) November 19, 2026

Guillemet said the transition had been in preparation for several months, adding that Ledger's teams, partners, and product roadmaps were ready for the change.

"We’ve been preparing this transition for many months, so Ledger’s teams, partners and roadmaps are ready. I’m bullish on Ledger’s future."

Ledger's Security Chief Warns of Growing AI-Powered Cyber Threats

Guillemet played a central role in developing Ledger's security infrastructure, most notably through the creation of Ledger Donjon in 2018. The company's attack laboratory focuses on identifying vulnerabilities in hardware and software before malicious actors can exploit them.

Your Ledger does more than secure your crypto. It now secures your entire digital life.🔐 With Ledger Security Key, your Ledger device becomes a robust security tool for websites that support passkeys, two-factor, or multi-factor authentication, like Google, Binance, and X. No passwords. No 2FA codes. No phishing risks. Set it up in minutes via Ledger Live — and watch the Ledger tutorial below for a full step-by-step walkthrough below👇

— Ledger (@Ledger) May 16, 2025

According to Guillemet, Ledger devices now secure approximately 20% of the world's cryptocurrency assets, highlighting the company's significant position in the digital asset security industry.

However, he warned that the cybersecurity landscape has changed considerably, with artificial intelligence making malicious attacks cheaper, faster, and easier to scale.

"The threat landscape changed too. AI is making attacks cheaper, faster and easier to scale."

He also suggested that the security challenges Ledger has spent nearly a decade addressing are no longer limited to cryptocurrency users.

"The question we spent a decade answering for crypto (how do you protect what matters when any device can be compromised?) is now a question for every company, every AI agent and every government."

🚨 BREAKING: HACKERS TARGETED 178 GLOBAL ORGANIZATIONS, STEALING CRYPTO AND PAYMENT DATA, WITH HSBC, BBC, CNN, ZOOM AND LEDGER AMONG THE AFFECTED A massive cyberattack exploited Optimizely, a third-party website platform, to inject malicious code into websites operated by 178 organizations worldwide. The attack turned trusted websites into potential gateways for cryptocurrency theft, credit card skimming and mobile device exploitation. The scale of the incident is alarming: 178 organizations affected • 188 infected JavaScript snippets identified • 1,611 Optimizely snippets examined • 32 banking and financial organizations affected • 23 technology and SaaS companies affected • 20 retail and fashion organizations affected Major organizations identified include HSBC, BBC, CNN, Zoom, Fox News, Ledger, Equifax, Salesforce, IKEA, GitLab and Air France-KLM. The financial damage and stolen data: Report URI identified approximately $7,040 in cryptocurrency received by attacker-controlled wallets: • Bitcoin: $5,380 • Litecoin: $762 • TRON: $719 • Ethereum: $100 • BNB Chain: $82 These are approximate reported wallet receipts, not the confirmed total financial losses. But cryptocurrency wasn’t the only target. The malicious scripts were designed to steal: • Credit card numbers, expiration dates and CVV codes • Browser cookies and session-related information • Screenshots of webpages • Cryptocurrency wallet addresses The malware could also replace legitimate wallet addresses with attacker-controlled addresses, potentially redirecting transactions before users realized what happened. iPhone users were also in the crosshairs. The attackers deployed two sophisticated exploit kits: • Coruna, targeting iOS 13–17 • DarkSword, targeting iOS 18 A separate iOS 26 exploit chain was also observed in a fingerprinting stage. Successful compromise of individual devices has not been established. The banking sector was hit hardest. HSBC websites across 11 markets appeared in the affected list, including the US, Hong Kong, Singapore, Australia, Mexico, UAE, Malaysia, Taiwan, Vietnam, Egypt and the Philippines. What happened next? Optimizely blocked the vulnerable signup pathway, deployed security fixes, removed malicious code, revoked access tokens and reset affected accounts. Report URI observed infected snippets falling dramatically during the cleanup, from 169 to just one remaining by 21:52 UTC on November 16. The bigger lesson is terrifying: Hackers didn’t need to breach 178 companies individually. They exploited one trusted third-party platform and used legitimate websites as potential distribution channels for malicious code. Your bank, your favorite news website or a cryptocurrency platform can look completely legitimate while a compromised third-party script operates in the background. This is how dangerous modern supply-chain attacks have become.

— Mr. Whale (@MrWhale) November 17, 2026

His comments highlight how AI is expanding the cybersecurity threat landscape, potentially exposing businesses, governments, and digital infrastructure to increasingly sophisticated attacks.

Departure Follows Recent Ledger Hardware Wallet Tampering Cases

Guillemet's planned departure comes just weeks after Ledger disclosed incidents involving genuine hardware wallets that had allegedly been modified with hidden components designed to capture users' recovery phrases.

The compromised devices were reportedly distributed through authorized resellers, raising concerns about the security of hardware wallets and the potential risks within cryptocurrency supply chains.

JUST IN: UP CLOSE VIDEO SHOWS HOW HACKERS STOLE OVER $80,000,000 SILENTLY CORRUPTING LEDGER #BITCOIN WALLETS A SCAM SHOP IN MALAYSIA WAS LISTED AS AN "OFFICIAL AUTHORIZED RESELLER FOR YEARS" BEHIND THE SCENES, CRIMINALS WERE INSERTING MICROSCOPIC SPY CHIPS ON EVERY WALLET THEY REPACKAGED THE DEVICE AND SHIPPED IT TO UNSUSPECTING VICTIMS ALL THE WHILE IT WAS SILENTLY CAPTURING THEIR PRIVATE KEYS THIS IS WILD ‼️

— The Bitcoin Historian (@pete_rizzo_) October 11, 2026

The first tampering incidents were reported in Asia, before subsequent cases emerged in Europe and the United Arab Emirates.

The disclosures underscore the importance of hardware security in an industry where users rely on self-custody devices to protect their digital assets. Recovery phrases are particularly sensitive because anyone who obtains them may be able to gain control of the associated cryptocurrency wallets.

Ledger CEO：每个人迟早都会遭到黑客攻击 2026 年 11 月 11 日，硬件钱包厂商 Ledger 首席执行官 Pascal Gauthier @_pgauthier 在接受 Bloomberg Television @BloombergTV 采访时，被问及如何让用户相信 Ledger 设备的安全性。他表示，世上没有绝对的安全，Ledger 和其他机构一样，也可能遭到黑客攻击。他称，此次损失约占 Ledger 所保护资产的 0.01%，而硬件钱包行业的损失金额和占比均低于中心化机构，因此他仍认为去中心化的安全模式更可靠。他也提到，市场仍需要银行和币安，行业面临的安全威胁将一年比一年严峻。 来源：Bloomberg Television

— 吴说区块链 (@wublockchain12) November 12, 2026

Despite his upcoming departure, Guillemet said he remains optimistic about Ledger's future. He did not reveal details about his next project but indicated that he intends to establish a new venture focused on addressing broader cybersecurity challenges.

His departure will close a nine-year chapter at Ledger, where he helped establish the company's security operations and advance its efforts to protect cryptocurrency assets. His next venture, meanwhile, could see him tackle a much broader challenge as AI continues to reshape the cybersecurity landscape.

data.title: Fraud Networks Exploit Verified Identities As APAC Accounts Become A Growing Target For Crypto Crime
data.description:
Verified Accounts Become A Growing Weakness As Fraud Networks Target Crypto Platforms

Passing identity checks no longer guarantees that an account is safe, as fraudsters increasingly use verified identities to move illicit funds.

Sumsub's Identity Fraud Report 2026–2027 found that 2.4% of approved users in Asia Pacific (APAC) were linked to detected fraud networks, with roughly one-third of these connections emerging only after users had passed identity verification.

The findings suggest that criminals are increasingly buying, renting or taking over legitimate accounts to operate money mule networks.

APAC accounted for 33% of all fraud networks detected worldwide, the highest share among regions analysed by Sumsub.

We know #GTAVI drops in two days. So before everyone becomes mysteriously unavailable, a quick update on the crime happening outside Vice City.
Our Identity Fraud Report 2026–27 is here. 🦾

This year, we investigated how AI is changing fraud—and who’s authorizing the agents… pic.twitter.com/xXRh2FQeku

— Sumsub (@sumsub) November 17, 2026

Fraud Becomes More Complex Despite Lower Detection Rates

Although global identity fraud fell 28% year on year to 1.6% in 2026, detected deepfake fraud increased by 31%.

Sumsub also recorded an increase in fraud complexity, as criminals increasingly rely on artificial intelligence, manipulated documents and coordinated account networks.

In cryptocurrency, the fraud rate on Sumsub's platform edged down from 2.2% to 2.1%, but its Fraud Complexity Index rose 16%.

Digitally edited identity documents increased by 88%, while identity mismatches climbed 19%.

Penny Chai, Sumsub's vice president for APAC, said that exchanges must continue monitoring accounts after onboarding rather than relying solely on initial identity checks.

"Fraudsters aren't just trying to get past the front door anymore. An account that was legitimate on day one may not be by month six, so exchanges need to keep checking identity against how the account actually behaves over time."

Regional figures also revealed different risks.

Japan's fraud rate surged 219% to 5.1%, while Singapore's fell 36% to 1%.

However, Singapore's fraud complexity index increased 9% to 2.13, and Hong Kong recorded a 72% rise in deepfake fraud.

Money Mule Networks Draw Greater Regulatory Attention

The scale of organised fraud has increased pressure on authorities across APAC.

Sumsub found that only 25% of surveyed businesses in the region used fraud network analysis to identify connections between suspicious accounts.

Thailand's licensed digital asset operators had suspended 62,516 suspected mule accounts by 31 July 2026, according to the Prime Minister's Office.

Government blocks 62,516 crypto accounts linked to financial crime

Authorities have blocked 62,516 cryptocurrency accounts used to launder criminal proceeds as part of a broader crackdown on online financial crime, government spokeswoman Rachada Dhnadirek said.

The accounts… pic.twitter.com/x6A51ZsK6M

— Thai Enquirer (@ThaiEnquirer) August 17, 2026

Meanwhile, Singapore's Scams (Countermeasures) and Other Matters Act 2026 allows police to disable scam-linked accounts and criminalises supplying or purchasing accounts for scam activities.

The wider threat is also reflected in regional losses.

The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime estimated that Southeast Asia-based scam groups caused between $88.3 billion and $114.1 billion in losses during 2025.

UN: Asia-Pacific lost up to US114bntoscamgangsin2025ascrimenetworksexpandglobally

PeopleacrossEastAsia,SoutheastAsia,AustraliaandNewZealandlostUS88.3 billion-114.1 billion to online scams in 2025 as transnational crime groups evolved into an… pic.twitter.com/xvcX0WL67w

— Thai Enquirer (@ThaiEnquirer) July 21, 2026

AI Agents Create Another Security Gap

Sumsub also warned that AI agents are introducing new risks as businesses allow automated systems to carry out transactions and other activities.

Its survey found that 61% of APAC businesses had detected or suspected fraud involving AI agents, but only 15% could suspend or revoke an agent's access.

Globally, 30% of businesses affected by agent-related fraud reported cases involving agents initiating purchases, payments or transfers.

A cryptocurrency-related incident in May demonstrated the risks, after an attacker reportedly used prompt injection to manipulate Grok into issuing a transfer command executed by the Bankr trading bot, draining approximately $170,000.

Bankr later restricted its system following another attack involving 14 user wallets.

1 Week ago 14 wallets drained around $2.1M stolen AI trading bot suspended

Execute trades via X (Twitter) commands
No human approval needed for transactions
Auto executes swaps transfers… pic.twitter.com/FfhExWnnaj

— Brain Master (@Brainmaster) May 27, 2026

Sumsub expects businesses to prioritise stronger identity checks, fraud network detection and controls over AI agents in 2027.

Its research also found that 74% of crypto businesses now consider verification accuracy important, compared with 39% prioritising faster onboarding.

The report draws on more than 5.8 million fraud samples and surveys of over 1,400 fraud and risk professionals and 1,500 consumers across 21 markets.

data.title: Anthropic went public but its stock price hasn't gone up: Is the crypto market really doomed?
data.description:
On the evening of November 18th, Anthropic set its IPO price at $83 per share, selling approximately 980 million shares and raising $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion IPO in June to become the largest IPO in US stock market history. Based on full dilution, its market capitalization was approximately $1.5 trillion, significantly lower than the $2 trillion rumored in the summer. ANT opened at $111.50, 34% higher than the IPO price, and reached a high of $114.99 during the day, briefly exceeding a market capitalization of $2 trillion, but closed at $1.4 trillion. Following its IPO, Anthropic has surpassed Nvidia to become the company with the highest market capitalization per capita in the US stock market (Technology Company Showdown: China Responsible for Artificial Intelligence, the US for AI?). Bitcoin has fallen from its high of $87,000 on September 23 to around $62,000, a drop of about 30%. Many in the industry blame ANT, especially CZ, who believes this is the most likely reason for the decline. In June, SpaceX went public, and the cryptocurrency community hoped to use tokenization to encourage users to participate in the IPO. However, on the day of the IPO, Binance Wallet, Bybit, Bitget Wallet, and MEXC all canceled their activities because their shared upstream provider, xStocks, did not acquire enough underlying shares.

At the time, Binance attracted $557 million USDC from approximately 27,700 addresses, and ultimately refunded all of it, only issuing tokens worth $1 million in replacements; the total orders across several platforms reportedly exceeded $1 billion.

Kraken, having received its tokens, only gave each transaction user a little over 4 SPCXx. Tokenized stocks, after six months of development, are performing similarly to SpaceX in Anthropic's initial public offerings. Gate may be maintaining a high success rate of 5% through special channels. Kraken and Bitget's success rates are still slightly over one percent, while Binance continues to refund all principal and then airdrop. It seems the crypto world is still the same as always; no wonder so many people have already prepared their apology announcements in advance. Meanwhile, Xstock, still acting like a Class A criminal, continues to make excuses, claiming it's taking food from the mouths of the wealthy. Recently, besides its upcoming IPO, Anthropic has also been making headlines at this year's APEC summit. Many big names who traveled thousands of miles to China to attend the conference had their accounts banned simply for using their Claude accounts... However, some people are still trying to find excuses for today's market volatility. For example, some believe that the announcement of short selling against AMD further shook the AI ​​industry. In March 2025, Inspur Information was added to the U.S. Entity List. However, Hunterbrook discovered that Inspur Information had since used at least six updated versions of AMD firmware, the most recent update being on October 19, 2026. As a result, AMD's stock price plummeted by 10%! Some say it's because of the Federal Reserve's actions. At 3:00 AM Beijing time on Thursday, a 15-page summary of the Fed's October meeting showed that if inflation cannot be controlled, a 50 basis point rate hike may be necessary in December! The peace declaration issued by the Chinese, Russian, and US leaders during this APEC summit also highlighted the US's main demand for stabilizing oil prices. Therefore, oil prices are currently trending downwards, and inflation should be able to stabilize. With the funds attracted by the Anthropic IPO now being returned, and the market continuing its downward trend, it might really be heading for a crash...

data.title: With a post-investment valuation of $1.5 billion, what makes Variational stand out?
data.description:
Tao Zhu, Jinse Finance

Summary:On November 18, 2026, the decentralized derivatives trading protocol Variational announced the completion of a $110 million Series B funding round, reaching a post-money valuation of $1.5 billion. This article will summarize Variational's specific information from aspects such as project background, founding team, token economics, and unique features.

I. Variational Completes $110 Million Series B Funding Round

On November 18, Variational officially announced the completion of a $110 million Series B funding round, reaching a post-money valuation of $1.5 billion. This round of financing was led by Bain Capital Crypto, with participation from Dragonfly, HSG, Peak XV, 50T Funds, and other institutions.

According to Variational's announcement (https://www.variational.io/blog/series-b), this round of funding will primarily be used to increase the open interest limit on the Omni platform, expand the range of trading instruments in the stock, index, commodity, and foreign exchange markets, and further expand its liquidity cooperation network with traditional financial institutions. Variational stated that since its launch in 2025, its Omni trading platform has accumulated a trading volume exceeding $475 billion, with over 100,000 accounts and an open interest exceeding $1.3 billion. Currently, traditional financial market assets account for more than half of the platform's daily trading volume. It is worth noting that Variational has previously received multiple rounds of funding: in October 2024, Variational completed a $10.3 million seed round; in May 2026, it completed a $50 million Series A funding round led by Dragonfly.

II. Variational Overview

1. Introduction to the Variational Protocol

According to the Variational official website, Variational is a protocol for on-chain derivatives trading, covering cryptocurrencies, stocks, commodities, and forex. By aggregating the deepest possible liquidity from centralized exchanges (CEXs), decentralized exchanges (DEXs), and traditional financial (TradFi) traders, Variational directly connects DeFi to the global economy.

The Variational Protocol currently supports two applications: Omni (a zero-fee personal trading venue) and Pro (a custom derivatives settlement layer for institutions).

Omni is an application built on the Variational protocol. It allows users to trade perpetual contracts between cryptocurrency and traditional markets within the same cross-margin account.

Omni is an application built on the Variational protocol. It allows users to trade perpetual contracts between cryptocurrency and traditional markets within the same cross-margin account.

  • Zero Fees:Omni does not charge transaction fees. By vertically integrating its liquidity providers, Omni retains market-making revenue that would otherwise be taken by external market makers.

  • TradFi-Level Liquidity Depth:Omni's liquidity providers are directly connected to centralized exchanges (CEXs), decentralized exchanges (DEXs), and traditional financial dealers, providing the narrowest possible bid-ask spreads across various crypto asset and traditional financial markets.

  • Hundreds of Trading Markets:Omni supports far more trading markets than traditional order book exchanges by integrating existing liquidity (rather than building new order books from scratch). Currently, the platform features over 500 crypto asset and traditional financial markets, with more continuously being added.

Pro's mission is to eliminate these inefficient steps and significantly simplify the institutional OTC derivatives trading process; by improving price discovery mechanisms and enhancing market accessibility, it unlocks billions of dollars in trading volume.

Pro automates the entire institutional trading process—covering every step from order placement, clearing to settlement—and migrates the entire process on-chain. Institutions can create highly customized derivatives, set specific margin and clearing rules, hold collateral in independent on-chain contracts, and use the Variational Oracle for pricing.

Pro offers the same level of customization as direct channels while maintaining the efficiency of an automated on-chain system.

2. Who are the founders of Variational?

Variational was co-founded by Lucas Schuermann and Edward Yu. The two met while studying at Columbia University, where they were both engineering students and researchers; in 2017, they founded their own hedge fund, Qu Capital.

In 2019, Qu Capital was acquired by Digital Currency Group, and Lucas and Edward subsequently became VP of Engineering and VP of Quantitative Trading, respectively, at Genesis Trading. In 2021, after handling hundreds of billions of dollars in trading volume at Genesis Trading (then one of the largest cryptocurrency trading platforms), Lucas and Edward left to found their own proprietary trading firm, Variational. After raising $10 million and successfully operating their trading strategy for several years (and gaining access to almost all centralized and decentralized exchanges in the space), Lucas and Edward decided to leverage Variational's trading profits to develop the Variational Protocol.

3. Variational Roadmap

Q2 2024:

  • Omni Testnet Launch

Q3 2024:

  • New Order Types: Take Profit/Stop Loss (TP/SL) and Limit Orders

  • Automated Listing Engine

Q4 2024:

  • Isolated Settlement Pools (Isolated settlement pools)

2024:

  • Isolated settlement pools (Isolated settlement pools)

  • Portfolio and Markets Page

  • Security Audit

  • Production Environment Load Testing and Scaling

    • Q1 2025:

    • Omni Private Mainnet Launch

    • Omni Referral Program Small-Scale Launch

    Q2 2025:

    • Leaderboard Page

    • Profit/Loss (PnL) Display Card

    • Omni Referral Program Fully Launch

    Q3 2025:

    • Configurable leverage

    • Display estimated liquidation price

    • Supports setting take-profit/stop-loss (TP/SL) trigger prices (based on the latest transaction price, mark price, or index price)

    • Major UI redesign (“Omni v2”)

    Q4 2025:

    • Pricing mechanism upgrade to narrow bid-ask spreads

    • New order type: Trigger Order (Trigger) Order)

    • Open Referral Rewards Claim Function

    • Support Adjusting Take-Profit/Stop-Loss/Limit/Trigger Orders by Dragging on the Chart

    • Launch Omni Points Program

    Other Roadmap Projects (Completed):

    • Open Read-Only Omni API

    • Optimize Mobile Experience

    • Support CSV Data Export

    • Launch RWA (Real-World Asset) Market and Integrate Native Crypto Liquidity (“Phase 1”)

    • Optimize Data Analysis Functionality on the “Portfolio” Page

    • Major UI Redesign (“Omni v3”)

    • Isolated Margin (Isolated) Margin) Mode

    • Protocol Statistics Page

    • Introducing Swap Functionality (“Phase Two”)

    • Omni Public Mainnet Launch

    4. Swaps—Bringing Traditional Financial Liquidity On-Chain

    Variational launched Swaps in September 2026, initially with Gold XAU and Nasdaq 100 Index US100, attempting to directly bring liquidity from traditional financial institutions into the on-chain derivatives market.

    Swaps is a key tool for realizing Variational’s long-term vision: through a unified cross-asset margin account covering cryptocurrencies, stocks, commodities, indices, and various currencies; this account provides execution quality comparable to traditional prime brokers while achieving the instant settlement capabilities of DeFi.

    According to Variational (https://www.variational.io/blog/introducing-swaps), Swaps differ from perpetual contracts in several key aspects: **Significantly Narrow Bid-Ask Spreads:** Because swaps hedge directly through traditional financial dealers rather than relying on aggregated crypto-native liquidity, their bid-ask spreads are much narrower than perpetual contracts, and their liquidity is also much deeper. This advantage is particularly pronounced when order sizes are large or the underlying asset trading volume is low. **Higher Open Interest (OI) Limits:** We have signed agreements to lock up over $1 billion in open interest (OI) in the swaps market. These limits will continue to increase as OLP connects with more traditional financial partners. Stable Financing Costs: Most swap contracts do not use floating funding rates, but instead have predictable holding costs (currently around 4.5% based on USD borrowing rates), while users also have the opportunity to earn dividends. Trading Hours: Initially, swap contract trading hours will align with traditional markets (e.g., $XAU-SWAP will be suspended for one hour daily). We are actively working with other platforms outside of trading hours to achieve 24/7 pricing for OLP swap contracts in the near future. Leveraging a Variational Broker-like Model: Swap contracts are over-the-counter (OTC) instruments. Such tools are not available on exchanges based on Central Limit Order Books (CLOBs); however, OLP, with its unique ability to act as a counterparty to traditional financial dealers (TradFi dealers), enables the trading of such contracts on-chain.

    III. Variational Token and Airdrop Status

    On September 24, Variational announced its token VAR Economics. According to official information, VAR is scheduled for TGE in Q4 2026, at which time an initial airdrop of 32% of the total supply will take place. Prior to TGE, tokens will continue to be distributed weekly. The specific allocation is as follows: Initial Airdrop [32%]: Airdropped based on the proportion of tokens held by users. This portion of tokens will be 100% unlocked at TGE. Ecosystem Reserve [18%]: Reserved by the Variational Foundation to support ecosystem growth; the specific allocation is determined by the Foundation. Team and Investors [50%]: Reserved for investors and current and future team members involved in building Variational. This portion of tokens will be locked for 12 months after TGE, and then gradually unlocked over at least three years. Team members will also be subject to their respective vesting arrangements. The specific allocation ratio between the team and investors will be announced before TGE. Variational plans to use all revenue entering the treasury to buy back and burn VAR tokens. IV. Differences between Variational and other DEXs 1. Different Trading Models Hyperliquid uses an on-chain Centralized Limit Order Book (CLOB) model, where traders can submit limit orders or market orders, and the system matches buyers and sellers according to the principle of price priority and time priority; Jupiter Perps mainly uses the AMM model, where liquidity pools act as counterparties for user transactions, and traders trade with liquidity pools; Variational's Omni uses the RFQ model, where after a user submits a trading request, the platform provides a quote through the Omni Liquidity Provider (OLP), and the user completes the transaction after accepting the quote. 2. **Different Sources of Liquidity** Traditional DEXs typically source liquidity from market makers in on-chain order books or funds in AMM liquidity pools. Variational's core liquidity provider, OLP, not only quotes prices to users but also hedges its own risks through centralized exchanges, decentralized exchanges, and over-the-counter markets. 3. **Different Trading Categories** Variational recently raised $110 million, which will primarily be used to increase the open interest limit on the Omni platform, expand the trading categories in stocks, indices, commodities, and forex markets, and further expand its liquidity cooperation network with traditional financial institutions. Hyperliquid and Jupiter, on the other hand, initially focused on crypto assets. Variational aims to become a bridge connecting the crypto market and traditional financial markets.

data.title: CZ Japan Interview: Don't Treat Lifetime Employment as the Only Career Option
data.description:
Author | PIVOT

Translation | Wu Shuo Blockchain

This issue features an interview with Binance founder CZ (Changpeng Zhao) by the Japanese business media PIVOT. CZ reviewed the founding and early development of Binance, as well as the important role Japan has played in his career. He believes that Japan is gradually improving its cryptocurrency regulatory environment, lowering tax rates, developing a yen stablecoin, and promoting asset tokenization, which is expected to attract more entrepreneurs and capital.

Regarding his previous legal cases and imprisonment in the United States, CZ explained his reasons for choosing to go to the US to resolve the issues. After leaving his management position at Binance, he will devote more energy to investment and the free education project Giggle Academy, hoping to expand educational opportunities through digital technology.

Regarding the future of the industry, CZ believes that the Internet, blockchain, and AI are the three most important technological changes of the past few decades.

As AI agents gradually replace humans in completing transactions, payments, and other tasks, traditional bank accounts and credit cards may struggle to meet the high-frequency, low-value transaction demands between machines. Crypto is poised to become a crucial payment infrastructure for the AI-native economy. He predicts that the combination of AI and blockchain could significantly alter transaction methods and economic activities within the next five years or so.

From Tokyo Programmer to Binance Founder: How Japan Influenced CZ's Career

PIVOT: Where do you live now? What special significance does Japan hold for your career?

CZ: I mainly live in Abu Dhabi now, but I travel frequently for work and also enjoy Japan, going skiing in Hokkaido almost every winter. My first job after graduating from university was in Tokyo, where I was involved in developing a securities trading system, primarily using C++ programming. This experience gave me a deep understanding of the technical architecture of exchanges and laid the foundation for founding Binance later. Including subsequent trips to Japan, I've lived in Japan for about six or seven years.

PIVOT: Why did Binance initially choose Japan as its development base?

CZ: Binance was founded in Shanghai in July 2017, but six weeks later China introduced regulatory policies targeting ICOs and cryptocurrency exchanges. At that time, Japan had just implemented a registration system for cryptocurrency exchanges, and we believed that Japan was ahead in terms of regulation, so we moved our team of about 30 people to Tokyo. However, the Japanese regulatory system differed from Binance's business model. At that time, Japanese exchanges could usually only list a dozen to twenty mainstream crypto assets, while Binance mainly offered a large number of altcoins for trading, so we did not stay in Japan for long. Later, Binance re-entered the Japanese market through its local licensed business. Japan's Crypto Tax Reform: Can Lower Tax Rates Attract More Funds? PIVOT: Japan is pushing for cryptocurrency tax reform, planning to reduce the tax rate from a maximum of about 55% to around 20%. What do you think of these changes? CZ: I think this is a very positive change. A capital gains tax rate of around 20% is similar to the tax treatment for Japanese stock investments and is internationally competitive, potentially attracting more trading volume back to Japan. However, unlike stocks, crypto assets may also be widely used for payments in the future. If crypto payments become truly widespread, Japan may need to further consider how to handle consumption tax and other transaction-related taxes. PIVOT: Is Japan's regulatory environment sufficient to attract more crypto entrepreneurs? CZ: Japan has always had relatively clear regulatory rules, but from around 2017 to 2021, there were indeed many restrictions, causing some entrepreneurs to leave. In the past few years, Japan has gradually reopened, and both domestic and overseas startup teams have begun to refocus on this market. I believe Japan should further encourage entrepreneurs to utilize crypto financing. Token financing can lower the financing threshold for startups. Although there are issues such as fraud and rg pulls, this should not negate the entire model. Japan has many excellent and dedicated entrepreneurs. If regulation can strike a balance between protecting investors and supporting innovation, it has the opportunity to attract more funding and projects.

Japanese Yen Stablecoins and RWA: What are Governments Most Concerned About?

PIVOT: You've communicated with governments of many countries. What are their biggest concerns regarding the crypto industry?

CZ: There are two main areas. The first is the regulation of crypto exchanges and stablecoins, and the second is asset tokenization.

Almost every country wants to tokenize its assets, including stocks, government bonds, real estate, and various physical resources. Some countries are even considering tokenizing assets like water resources to finance infrastructure construction by selling future resource supplies in advance.

Stock tokenization follows a similar logic. If the stocks of Japanese listed companies can be more easily purchased by global investors, it could increase liquidity and attract more funds for Japanese companies. Stablecoins can be understood as the tokenization of the domestic currency.

PIVOT: Japan already has Japanese yen stablecoins like JPYC. How can this be truly scaled up?

CZ: The yen is an important global currency, but currently, almost all stablecoins in the crypto market are based on the US dollar.

I believe Japan should more actively promote the development of yen-denominated stablecoins. Japan is characterized by cautious initial decision-making, but once a direction is confirmed, it can quickly implement and scale up. Exchange regulation has gone through a similar process in the past, and stablecoins may now be at a turning point. Besides stablecoins, Japan should also further promote the tokenization of assets such as stocks, ETFs, and government bonds. Responding to the US legal case: Why did you choose to go to the US to resolve the issue? PIVOT: In 2023, you pleaded guilty to Binance's US operations and anti-money laundering compliance issues, subsequently resigned as CEO, and served four months in prison in 2024. How do you view this experience now? CZ: Binance did have US users between 2017 and 2019, but at that time, we did not complete the relevant registration as required, which involved violating the US Bank Secrecy Act. This is a fact I admit. At the time, I was in the UAE and could have chosen to stay there, but I didn't want to keep avoiding the issue, so I decided to go to the US to resolve it and ultimately accepted the plea bargain. I believe my punishment is somewhat unique compared to similar compliance cases at some traditional financial institutions, but different cases have different backgrounds. My guilty plea involved violations of the Bank Secrecy Act, not fraud. This experience has taught me many lessons, but I don't want to dwell on the past. Leaving my management role at Binance has given me more time to freely choose what I consider valuable. Currently, Binance is managed by another team, and I focus my energy on areas like investment and education. Giggle Academy: Why Free Education? PIVOT: After leaving Binance, you started working at Giggle Academy. Why education? CZ: I believe finance and education share a common goal: to provide more opportunities for people. Financial services allow people to manage assets and participate in economic activities, while education allows people to learn and improve their lives. Globally, a large number of adults are still illiterate, and hundreds of millions of children lack access to formal education. Traditional education systems also have problems, such as overemphasizing average performance across all subjects rather than fully developing individual strengths. With AI, mobile internet, and gaming technology, we can now provide free education to children worldwide through a single app. Giggle Academy is built on this idea. We've been developing it for about two years, with courses starting for children around two years old and currently covering children around six. In early 2026, the platform had approximately 100,000 children using it; now it has grown to about 2 million. My long-term goal is to serve 100 million children, or even more. How will Giggle Academy maintain its free operation in the long term? PIVOT: Giggle Academy doesn't have subscriptions or in-app purchases. How will it maintain its operation? The marginal cost of digital education is very low; even if the user base grows significantly in the future, the operating costs will not increase proportionally. Why AI Agents Need Crypto: Future Payments Could Grow a Thousandfold PIVOT: You are currently investing in AI, Web3, and biotechnology. How do you think AI and Crypto will combine? CZ: Over the past few decades, I believe the three most important technological changes have been the internet, blockchain, and AI. AI will impact almost every industry, significantly improving productivity, and we may only be beginning to understand its potential. In the future, there may be hundreds or thousands of AI agents working behind every individual. For example, after an interview, different agents could be responsible for editing, publishing, promoting, and charging, generating a large number of transactions and payment needs among them. However, AI agents are unlikely to use credit cards or traditional bank accounts like humans. They can certainly operate bank accounts on behalf of humans, but for machine-to-machine transactions, a more natural solution is to use digital native currency, i.e., Crypto. I believe AI could increase transaction frequency a thousandfold, or even a millionfold, while making individual transaction amounts smaller. For example, in the future, watching a video might only require paying one yen, without having to purchase a full subscription. AI agents could automatically complete these micropayments. When a large number of agents begin to provide services, exchange data, and complete tasks with each other, micropayments may become ubiquitous. Traditional payment systems may not be suitable for such high-frequency, small-amount transactions, while blockchain and Crypto can provide a more suitable infrastructure. AI and blockchain will not only change payments but also identity authentication and asset transactions. PIVOT: Besides payments, what other directions are there for the integration of AI and blockchain? CZ: AI needs not only currency, but also digital identity, authentication, and verification mechanisms, all of which can be combined with blockchain. For example, when buying property in the future, users can view historical transaction records, asset ownership, and other relevant information through a digital system. If this data can be reliably recorded and verified, AI can help users quickly analyze and process it, significantly improving transaction efficiency. I believe that the combination of AI and blockchain will significantly increase the frequency of transactions throughout society, making economic activities more efficient. Payment is just one application; in the future, it may also involve asset ownership, identity authentication, and public services. PIVOT: How long do you think these changes will take?
